status: Experiment hypotheses for the lookup-v2 phase, derived from rtl-1. Not approved product settings. Every rtl-1 field keeps its value; rules marked 'changed' or H5+ are new and are enabled only by the fields of this file.
lemma_fallback_rule: H5: when neither the exact key nor the token key matches a dictionary expression, strip one regular inflection from the last word of the exact key and use the first resulting key that exists as a dictionary exact key (match_kind = lemma_fallback). Rule order: -s (not after s), -es, -ies -> -y, then -ing and -ed, each tried with e-restoration first (pars -> parse, which also covers -d), then bare, then with a doubled final consonant undoubled (runn -> run). Bases shorter than 3 letters are not tried. Candidates identical to the lemma's token key or index tokens are rejected as same_as_query.
repository_presence: H1 (changed for phrases): a single-index-token candidate is kept when its token has file_count >= 1, as in rtl-1. A multi-token candidate is kept only when its index tokens concatenated without a separator (event loop -> eventloop) have file_count >= 1 (phrase_evidence = concatenated), or when one of its non-excluded relation kinds is listed in phrase_evidence_relation_kinds and every component has file_count >= 1 (phrase_evidence = components_only). Otherwise it is rejected with reason phrase_without_identifier_evidence; the presence field still records component presence.
commonness_rule: H2: drop a single-index-token candidate whose live-file fraction exceeds the value. Multi-token candidates have no defined fraction and are not filtered. The value is a hypothesis; per-candidate counts are saved so other cutoffs can be recomputed without rerunning.
final_limit_rule: H3: at most this many final terms per input after deduplication; every earlier-stage candidate stays in the output. Morphology words never count toward this limit.
ordering: H4 (changed): relation-kind priority, then the query word's WordNet sense order (0 = most frequent; non-WordNet evidence = 0), then repository file count descending (single token: its count; multi-token: the concatenated identifier's count when present, else the smallest component count), then more supporting relations, then exact_key.
deduplication: Candidates with identical index-token sequences (for example 'publish-subscribe' and 'publish subscribe') collapse to the first in order.
not_ready_behavior: When repository statistics are not ready (stale, missing, incompatible, unavailable, not configured), no final terms are produced; dictionary candidates are still reported as not_evaluated, and morphology reports repository_not_ready with no words.
morphology_rule: H6: for a query with exactly one index token (ASCII letters, length >= 3), return published repository words that share the query's Snowball English stem (tantivy Stemmer, read from the index-time word_stems table), excluding the query itself, in a separate morphology list that is never mixed into dictionary candidates, final_terms, or final_limit. A word is typed inflection when, under the H5 suffix rules, it is an inflection base of the query, the query is its base, or both share a base (sibling inflections such as executing/executed); otherwise derivation. The list is ordered by file count descending (then word) and capped at morphology_limit. query_file_count and query_absent_in_repository are reported for every query.
morphology_prefix_rule: H7: prefix family typed same_root. (a) When the query starts with a listed prefix and the remainder has at least morphology_min_prefix_remainder_length letters, add published words sharing the remainder's stem (reconnect -> connect, connection). (b) For the query and each of its same-stem words, add prefix + word when that exact word has a word_stems row (lock, locked -> unlock, unlocked); this uses point lookups only, never a vocabulary scan. String prefixes are not morphemes: false families such as display/play are expected and measured, not filtered.
block_rule: H8: rtpoc2 block expands each input term that is not identifier-shaped (codemap-search split_identifier yields more than one token, or the term contains '::' or '.'); identifier-shaped terms pass through with reason identifier_shaped. Per expanded term it lists up to block_dictionary_terms_per_term final dictionary terms (relation kind plus the gloss of the first non-excluded evidence that has one, trimmed to block_gloss_max_chars) and up to block_morphology_words_per_term morphology words, filtered by --mode. The task query is recorded only.
suggested_query_rule: H9: expanded terms whose query is absent in the repository come first, then input order. Each term's replacements are taken in order (absent in repository: morphology then dictionary; otherwise dictionary then morphology) and each is combined with up to block_anchor_words_max anchors: the other input terms with the smallest positive repository file count, skipping anchors that would exceed block_query_max_words or repeat a word. Queries without an anchor or below block_query_min_words are skipped; duplicates by lowercase word set are dropped; generation stops at block_suggested_query_limit.
block_size_rule: H10: block_text never exceeds max_block_bytes. Lowest-ranked expansions are dropped first (latest rank position, later term on ties), then suggested queries from the end, then term lines from the end, and only then are bytes cut at a character boundary. Every omission is counted in block_omissions.
